newsitem.title: IRAN: Fast trials for fast wealth in Iran - ayatollah.
newsitem.headline: Fast trials for fast wealth in Iran - ayatollah.

text.p: One of Iran's leading clerics on Friday called for swift trials for people who have amassed legendary wealth overnight.
Ayatollah Ahmad Jannati, leading Friday prayers at Tehran university, said they must be brought to justice for their illegal practices.
He said conventional legal procedures in Iranian courts took too long for such cases to be efficient and such hearings must be speedy and revolutionary, the official news agency IRNA said.
Judicial processes that were too slow would be simply denial of justice, Janneti told thousands of worshippers at the university campus.

The Islamic republic's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei last week called for stepping up the fight against corruption and influence-peddling in Iran and rejected suggestions that tough action might discourage investors.
"There are people aiming to create a new privileged class in the Islamic Republic of Iran through connections, nominations, clever means...and access to public wealth," he said.
Iranian leaders have called for tough action against corruption following a series of trials for embezzlement and fraud at state agencies and banks in recent years.
Jannati said the issue was sensitive and demanded fully qualified as well as enterprising judges willing to carry out justice even though it should be at the cost of their own dismissal from the bar.

Investigations would need very bold people who should not be timid, who may not be bribed or hoodwinked and who would not listen to proposals of mercy or leniency towards the suspects. If not, the whole issue would be simply whitewashed, he said.
